```plato

    //==
    // # Ring predicates and repair
    //
    // `Polygon2D` declares simplicity — at least three vertices, no edge crossings —
    // as an invariant, and until now nothing in the tree could check it. These are
    // that check and the repairs that establish what is establishable, so that the
    // constructive operations above and in `triangulation.library.plato` can state
    // "precondition: simple" and have callers able to honour it.
    //
    // Conventions fixed here:
    //
    //   * Coincidence and collinearity are tested EXACTLY, with no tolerance. A
    //     tolerance would make these predicates disagree with the bodies that consume
    //     them, which are exact throughout, and would silently merge distinct vertices
    //     of a finely sampled ring. Callers wanting a tolerant answer should snap their
    //     input first.
    //   * The predicates are O(n^2): every pair of edges is tested. A sweep-line is
    //     the standard improvement and is separate, later work.
    //   * The repairs are TOTAL — every ring has an answer, including a degenerate one,
    //     which they reduce rather than reject. `RemoveCollinearVertices` of a
    //     zero-width spike is empty, and that is the honest result.

    // True when `q` lies on the segment [a, b], endpoints included: collinear with it
    // and within its bounding box.
    IsOnSegment(q: Point2D, a: Point2D, b: Point2D): Boolean
        => TwiceSignedArea(a, b, q) == 0.0
        && q.X >= a.X.Min(b.X) && q.X <= a.X.Max(b.X)
        && q.Y >= a.Y.Min(b.Y) && q.Y <= a.Y.Max(b.Y);

    // True when the segments [a, b] and [c, d] share at least one point — a proper
    // crossing, a touch at an endpoint, or a collinear overlap.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_segment_intersection
    SegmentsIntersect(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D, d: Point2D): Boolean
    {
        var aSide = TwiceSignedArea(c, d, a);
        var bSide = TwiceSignedArea(c, d, b);
        var cSide = TwiceSignedArea(a, b, c);
        var dSide = TwiceSignedArea(a, b, d);
        var proper = aSide != 0.0 && bSide != 0.0 && cSide != 0.0 && dSide != 0.0
            && (aSide > 0.0).ExclusiveOr(bSide > 0.0)
            && (cSide > 0.0).ExclusiveOr(dSide > 0.0);
        return proper
            || a.IsOnSegment(c, d) || b.IsOnSegment(c, d)
            || c.IsOnSegment(a, b) || d.IsOnSegment(a, b);
    }

    // True when ring edges `i` and `j` share a point they are not entitled to.
    // Adjacent edges are entitled to the vertex between them and nothing else, so for
    // them the test is whether either one's far endpoint lies on the other — which is
    // what a doubled-back spike or a repeated vertex looks like. Non-adjacent edges are
    // entitled to nothing. Precondition: i < j.
    RingEdgesInterfere(points: Array<Point2D>, i: Integer, j: Integer): Boolean
    {
        var a = points[i];
        var b = points.AtModulo(i + 1);
        var c = points[j];
        var d = points.AtModulo(j + 1);
        var sharesLast = j == i + 1;
        var sharesFirst = i == 0 && j == points.Count - 1;
        return sharesLast ? a.IsOnSegment(c, d) || d.IsOnSegment(a, b)
            : sharesFirst ? b.IsOnSegment(c, d) || c.IsOnSegment(a, b)
            : SegmentsIntersect(a, b, c, d);
    }

    // The number of edge pairs that interfere. Zero for a simple ring; offered
    // alongside `IsSimpleRing` because "how badly" is the useful question when a repair
    // is being considered.
    RingSelfIntersectionCount(points: Array<Point2D>): Integer
        => points.Count.Range.Reduce(0, (total, i)
            => total + points.Count.Range.Reduce(0, (row, j)
                => row + (j > i ? (points.RingEdgesInterfere(i, j) ? 1 : 0) : 0)));

    // True when the ring is a simple polygon: at least three vertices and no two edges
    // meeting anywhere they should not. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simple_polygon
    IsSimpleRing(points: Array<Point2D>): Boolean
        => points.Count >= 3 && points.RingSelfIntersectionCount == 0;

    // The ring traversed the other way round, which flips its winding.
    ReversedRing(points: Array<Point2D>): Array<Point2D>
        => points.Count.MapRange(i => points[points.Count - 1 - i]);

    // The ring wound counter-clockwise, reversed only if it was not. A degenerate ring
    // (zero signed area) is left alone: there is no orientation to correct.
    CounterClockwiseRing(points: Array<Point2D>): Array<Point2D>
        => points.ShoelaceArea < 0.0 ? points.ReversedRing : points;

    // The ring with every vertex that coincides with its successor dropped, the last
    // vertex being compared with the first.
    RingWithoutDuplicateVertices(points: Array<Point2D>): Array<Point2D>
    {
        var kept = new List<Point2D>();
        var i = 0;
        while (i < points.Count)
        {
            if (points[i].IsSamePoint(points.AtModulo(i + 1)).Not)
            {
                kept = kept.Add(points[i]);
            }
            i = i + 1;
        }
        return kept.Freeze();
    }

    // The ring with the vertex at position `i` removed.
    RingWithout(points: Array<Point2D>, i: Integer): Array<Point2D>
        => points.Take(i).Concatenate(points.Skip(i + 1));

    // The position of the first vertex whose corner encloses no area — a collinear
    // midpoint, or the tip of a zero-width spike — or -1 when the ring has none. A ring
    // below three vertices has no corners to speak of and reports -1.
    FirstFlatVertex(points: Array<Point2D>): Integer
        => points.Count < 3 ? -1
        : points.Count.Range.Reduce(-1, (found, i) => found >= 0 ? found
            : TwiceSignedArea(points.AtModulo(i + points.Count - 1), points[i],
                points.AtModulo(i + 1)) == 0.0 ? i : found);

    // The ring with every flat vertex dropped, ONE AT A TIME.
    //
    // Removing them in a single sweep is wrong, and wrong in a way that quietly changes
    // the region: a vertex that appears twice has zero turn at both copies — once from
    // the collinear run it sits in, once from the repeat — so a sweep deletes the corner
    // outright rather than reducing it to one vertex. Removing the first flat vertex and
    // re-examining is O(n^2) and correct, and correct wins here (STYLE_GUIDE.md).
    // Terminates because every step shortens the ring.
    RingWithoutCollinearVertices(points: Array<Point2D>): Array<Point2D>
    {
        var result = points;
        var flat = result.FirstFlatVertex;
        while (flat >= 0)
        {
            result = result.RingWithout(flat);
            flat = result.FirstFlatVertex;
        }
        return result;
    }

    //==
    // # Polygon2D predicates and repair

    // True when the polygon satisfies the invariant its declaration states.
    IsSimple(p: Polygon2D): Boolean
        => p.Points.IsSimpleRing;

    // How many edge pairs violate that invariant.
    SelfIntersectionCount(p: Polygon2D): Integer
        => p.Points.RingSelfIntersectionCount;

    // Which way the boundary winds. A degenerate ring reports CounterClockwise: there
    // is no better answer, and the repair below treats it as already correct.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding.
    Winding(p: Polygon2D): WindingOrder
        => p.Points.ShoelaceArea < 0.0 ? WindingOrder.Clockwise : WindingOrder.CounterClockwise;

    // The polygon wound counter-clockwise, so that it encloses positive area.
    EnsureCounterClockwise(p: Polygon2D): Polygon2D
        => Polygon2D(p.Points.CounterClockwiseRing);
```
